children: The central bank raised rates to 2.5% and didn't dispel expectations of three more hikes by April. Resilient euro zone growth has emboldened it to keep tightening. Yet with workers and firms swallowing the pain of high energy costs, a slowdown is a bigger risk than inflation.
Full view will be published shortly.
Follow Jon Sindreu on X and LinkedIn.
The European Central Bank on September 10 raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter of a percentage point to 2.5%, while also upgrading its projections for inflation and economic growth.

As of 1300 GMT on September 10, Brent oil prices and European natural gas prices traded at $104.80 per barrel and €83.07 per megawatt-hour, respectively. This is compared with $72.92 and €43.65 at the end of June, respectively.
